A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HadamRNN and Block-HadamRNN work. Both retain Appendices A-I, Tables 1-10, and Figures 1-3. The text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HadamRNN and Block-HadamRNN experiments in Tables 2-3, additional GLUE and IoT results in Appendix F, and original stability, ablation, and memory-perturbation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results and the experimental analyses in Appendices E-H. These include outcomes produced by the proposed models, not merely results attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The linear recurrence, Hadamard and block-Hadamard parameterizations, input/output quantization, STE training, and activation quantization are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C and I. Revised descriptions do not alter the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the copy task, pMNIST, sMNIST, IMDB, SST-2, QQP, HAR-2, and DSA-19. Although v3 newly names GLUE and IoT benchmarks in the abstract and introduction, their evaluations already appear in v1 Appendix F. The memory-perturbation scenario is also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 6, and 7 retain the same task-specific LSTM, ORNN, QORNN, FastGRNN, and quantized-BERT comparisons. The ablation comparators are also unchanged. Consolidating duplicate BiT references does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices D, F, G, and I retain the same splits, sequence lengths, preprocessing, model configurations, quantization settings, training budgets, metrics, perturbation procedure, and activation calibration. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the sparsity comparisons in Table 3, bitwidth/learning-rate stability analysis in Appendix E.2, linear-versus-ReLU ablation and memory experiment in Appendix G, and row/column-sign ablation in Appendix H. Their tested questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 in both versions specifies five models trained with five random seeds per bitwidth/learning-rate combination and reports averages and standard deviations in Table 5. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 6 retains 81.9% for HadamRNN on SST-2 and 82.1% for Block-HadamRNN on QQP, while Table 8 retains the ReLU variant's failure on the copy task. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, orthogonality proofs, memory analysis, sign-switch equivalence argument, and fixed-point derivations are retained. Appendix B.4 removes an extraneous parenthesis from a squared matrix-entry expression; this is a typesetting correction without changed mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The claims concerning binary and sparse-ternary ORNN construction, long-copy-task capability, compact storage, and computational tradeoffs remain the same. Explicitly listing the existing GLUE and IoT evaluations in the abstract and introduction changes emphasis, not the contribution's scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations based on orthogonality and linear recurrence, the sparsity-performance tradeoff, the exclusion of Long Range Arena, and the GLUE limitations involving overfitting and pretrained embeddings. Rewording adds no substantive mechanism explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, GPU disclosure, training times, fixed-point implementation details, and code link are unchanged. Section 3.6 more explicitly associates stored bits with the binary vector and input/output matrices, but this restates information already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds the characterization of Kusupati et al. (2018) as the only surveyed work solving IoT tasks. This is a limited positioning addition. The cited works otherwise remain the same; merging duplicate Liu et al. (2022) entries and shortening venue metadata are bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and grammar edits across the main text and selected appendices, expands the abstract/introduction's benchmark list, cleans up the bibliography, and adds a PhD-funding acknowledgment. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 8 to page 9, its caption is shortened, and tighter spacing changes the flow of the experiment discussion and conclusion. There are small caption and equation-formatting edits. All ten tables and three figures retain their substantive display content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves communication by making the existing evaluation scope explicit, clarifying storage accounting in Section 3.6, and correcting grammar, a malformed equation parenthesis, and duplicate references. The scientific evidence and reproducibility remain unchanged. Denser spacing and the merged Copy task heading in Section 4.1 introduce a small readability tradeoff.
